# Test fixtures

Static data behind the shared fake environment (`test/fake-env`), which copies it into a temporary folder for each test:

- `projects/`: fixture Projects. `harbor-api` declares a GitHub Tracker, `recipe-box` a local markdown Tracker, `dotfiles` declares none. `recipe-box/.scratch/` holds two Maps: `meal-planner` (open) has a Ticket of every type and every state (Frontier, claimed, blocked, closed), a Ticket blocked by two open Tickets, a redundant edge the transitive reduction drops, and a closed Ticket whose blocker is still open; `pantry-audit` is all closed; `ideas/` has no `map.md`, so it is not a Map.
- `claude-home/`: the Claude Code home (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`). `sessions/<project>/` holds Session histories for a fixture Project; `__CWD__` and `__CWD_JSON__` are replaced with the Project's path, and the files land in `projects/<encoded path>/` as Claude Code stores them. `sessions/<project>@<worktree>/` does the same for a git worktree of the Project, created at `<project>/.claude/worktrees/<worktree>` and linked as git links worktrees. A `*.live.json` file is a live-session registry entry, written to `sessions/<pid>.json` with `__LIVE_PID__` replaced by the test's own process id (a running `claude`) or `__DEAD_PID__` by the id of a process that has exited (an entry a crashed `claude` left behind).
- Extensions: `claude-home/skills/`, `claude-home/agents/` and `recipe-box/.claude/` hold the user's and recipe-box's own skills and subagents. `claude-home/plugins/cache/forge-market/` holds three installed plugins: `kitchen-tools` (the user's, enabled, with the `pantry` MCP server and a skill and a subagent both in its default folders and in folders its manifest names), `frontend-design` (installed for recipe-box only) and `atlas` (the user's, disabled).
- `claude/`: what the fake `claude` answers to its Extension commands. The fake environment copies it, and the fake changes the copy as `claude mcp add|remove` and `claude plugin install|uninstall|enable|disable` would change Claude Code's setup. A `hold-changes` file in the copy makes those commands wait, and a `fail-changes` file makes them fail with its text (`holdClaudeChanges()`, `failClaudeChanges()`).
  - `mcp-list/user.txt`, `mcp-list/<folder>.mcp-json.txt` then `mcp-list/<folder>.txt` are the server lines of `claude mcp list` run in a folder, as Claude Code prints them: the user's servers everywhere (user scope), then those a fixture Project shares in its `.mcp.json` (project scope) and the user's own in it (local scope), the narrower scope replacing a server of the same name. The user has a needs-sign-in server (`claude.ai Supabase`); recipe-box has a failed one (`playwright`); harbor-api shares one pending approval (`sentry`), and has one connected without its tools (`tracing`), one in a status ClaudeForge does not know (`metrics`) and its own `github`, replacing the user's.
  - `plugins.json` is `claude plugin list --json`, with `installPath` relative to the Claude Code home and `projectPath` naming a fixture Project; the fake fills in the paths and reports a Project's plugin enabled only in that Project's folder.
  - `plugins-available.json` is the `available` part of `claude plugin list --available --json`: the marketplaces' plugins, installed or not. `pastry-kit` installs from `marketplace/pastry-kit/` (with the `proofing` skill); `sentry-tools` fails to install with its `fakeInstallError`.
- `web/`: the pages a Web shortcut opens in the Shortcuts journeys, which serve them on this machine as a Project's dev server would: `index.html` sets a cookie lasting an hour (a sign-in kept across restarts), links to `pricing.html` and opens a link in a new window.
- `gh/`: what the fake `gh` replays (from the fake environment's copy, `ghRecordings`, which a test may change), shaped like real GitHub REST responses (recorded from a real repository, then rewritten to the fixture values).
  - `api/`: one file per path for `gh api <path>` (`gh api repos/fixture/harbor-api` reads `gh/api/repos/fixture/harbor-api.json`). A listing's recording is its first page (`page` 2 onwards is empty), and the issue list is filtered by its `state` and `labels`; other query parameters and `-f` fields pick nothing.
  - `repo-view/<folder>.json`: what `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,url` answers in a fixture Project's folder; a folder without one is not a GitHub repository.
  - harbor-api is `fixture/harbor-api`, and `gh` is signed in as `fixture-user`. Its Map #40 *Rate limiting* has sub-issues #41-#48 of every type and state: a Ticket claimed by `fixture-user` and one by `dana-reyes`, native blocks (`dependencies/blocked_by`), a closed Ticket (#46) whose blocker is still open, a `Blocked by:` body line naming a Ticket and an issue outside the Map (#30), and a block by an issue of another repository (`fixture/gateway#7`). Map #60 *Audit log* has no sub-issues and lists its Tickets as a task list, with `Part of #60` and `Blocked by:` lines. Map #70 *Webhooks* nests Sub-tickets two levels deep: Parent Ticket #71 (closed, claimed and Frontier Tickets beneath it, and Parent Ticket #75 holding #77) natively blocks #72, whose Sub-ticket #76 is blocked through it. Every sub-issue answers `issues/<n>/parent` with its parent issue, as GitHub does; an issue without one answers 404. Map #20 is closed.
- `az/`: what the fake `az` (with its `azure-devops` extension) replays (from the fake environment's copy, `azRecordings`, which a test may change), shaped like the real `az` answers for the organisation `https://devops.example.test/fixture-org`: `projects.json` (`az devops project list`), `areas.json` and `iterations.json` (the whole classification trees, from which `--path` picks a node and `--depth` cuts it) and `work-items.json` (`az boards query`, whatever the WIQL). `{{today}}`, `{{today+7}}` or `{{today-3}}` is that day, so the project Harbor's iteration root `Team Rocket` always has Sprint 41 behind, Sprint 42 running and Sprint 43 to come, in a year folder; its area `Platform & Ops` holds a `&` for cmd.exe to leave alone. The Work items have accented titles, a double quote and a percent sign, two assigned to the user (`System.AssignedTo` present) and a type of every glyph. A `mode` file answers as an `az` nobody signed in to (`signed-out`) or one without the extension (`no-extension`), as `setAzMode()` writes it.

Later tickets extend these fixtures (more Session kinds, Maps covering every Ticket state, Sub-tickets, Extensions).
